skeleton: woodpecker perched on its two feet, facing left: root at the feet; body with belly squash; head at the neck with a face bone carrying the two eyes (the far one peeking past the beak) and the long beak (closed/open); near wing folded on the back (open in flight), the far wing shown only open in flight (shaded, behind); legs on the root; stiff tail at the rump. A clinging pose (a clinging body, clinging feet, the tail braced down) swaps in for the trunk: the cling move and the tap/drum actions.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a woodpecker character. Draw this exact woodpecker as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the plump body with its cream speckled chest, standing upright as in image 1, without head, without tail, without legs and WITHOUT ANY WING: where the folded black-and-white spotted wing lies on its side in image 1, draw only plain black back feathers, no wing shape and no wing spots on it; its top, normally under the head, rounded.
2. the head: the head with its red crest, its black stripe and the red patch at the back of the neck, facing left as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no brow, no beak — keep the rosy cheek; its bottom edge rounded.
3. the folded wing: the black wing with its rows of white spots folded at rest, as it lies on the body in image 1, drawn whole, with a rounded shoulder at the top.
4. the open wing: the same wing spread wide as in flight, its black flight feathers with white spots fanned out, with a rounded shoulder at its base.
5. the tail: the long stiff black-and-white barred tail feathers, as in image 1, with a rounded base.
6. one leg: a grey scaly leg standing, as in image 1, from the top of the thigh (a rounded top) down to the foot with its toes and curved claws.
7. the clinging body: the same body as part 1 (cream chest, black back, no head, no wing, no tail, no legs, top rounded) but in the pose of a woodpecker clinging upright to a vertical tree trunk that is on its left: the body stretched upright and a little slimmer, straight up and down, its cream chest facing left towards the trunk, its black back on the right.
8. one clinging foot: the same grey scaly leg and foot as part 6 but gripping a vertical tree trunk that is on its left: a short leg with a rounded top, the toes reaching forward to the left and curled, the claws hooked as if holding on to bark.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No tree, no bark, no text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a woodpecker character; image 2 shows the same woodpecker cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the woodpecker's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the woodpecker in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in two tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the woodpecker's near eye as it is in image 1: a big dark round eye with white sparkles and a thin brown outline, with the small curved brow line above it.
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its sparkles, the brow raised.
3. the same eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few lashes, the same brow.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, the same brow.
5. the same eye sad: looking down, its brow tilted up towards the middle.
6. the beak as it is in image 1: long, straight, pointed and grey, closed, pointing left.
7. the same beak open, chirping: the upper and lower beak a little apart, pointing left.
8. the same beak wide open in a big yawn, pointing left, the inside pink.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the woodpecker taps its beak against the bark, tap-tap-tap, with little wood chips flying, then presses its eye close to listen for bugs, then taps once more and chirps happily.

pause.shows: the woodpecker listening, head tilted, one eye close to where it tapped

animations.description: the woodpecker flies along to the left with bouncy wingbeats, then lands and folds its wings.
the woodpecker clings upright to the bark, tail braced, gripping with its toes
the woodpecker drums on the tree trunk, rat-a-tat-tat, very fast, then leans back proudly with its eye closed happily.
the woodpecker opens its wings and flaps them, its feet staying where they are.

pause.shows: the woodpecker with its wings spread wide

animations.description: the woodpecker crouches, hops up with its wings out and lands with a little squash.
the woodpecker shakes its head no.
the woodpecker looks up, then turns right round to look behind it, then turns back and looks ahead again.

pause.shows: the woodpecker turned round, looking behind it

animations.description: the woodpecker laughs and laughs, bouncing with giggles.
the woodpecker does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side.
the woodpecker talks, its mouth moving, its head bobbing a little.
the woodpecker shivers and trembles, cold or scared.
the woodpecker cries, head down, shoulders shaking with little sobs.
the woodpecker gives a big yawn, closes its eyes and falls asleep, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.
